strategies.outdated: This analysis was written prior to Miraidon's ban. As such, the information provided is out of date and does not accurately reflect the current metagame. Bear with us while we rework our analyses!
strategies.overview: Arceus is debatably Ubers's most terrifying and dangerous setup sweeper thanks to a powerful STAB-boosted Extreme Speed, decent defenses, and a wide array of utility and coverage moves, letting it mix and match to win problematic matchups easily. Arceus also has an excellent defensive profile, allowing it to take on Ghost-types like Lunala and Flutter Mane. Extreme Speed allows Arceus to operate as a revenge killer, making it difficult for opposing setup sweepers like Scale Shot Koraidon, Miraidon, and Rayquaza to sweep. However, Arceus is not without its flaws, as physically bulky walls like Ting-Lu, Arceus-Water, and especially Necrozma-DM all check it and give it difficulty when attempting to sweep. Furthermore, while more uncommon, Arceus often struggles to beat bulky Ghost-types like Tera Ghost Koraidon, Tera Ghost Miraidon, Giratina-O, Lunala, and Skeledirge, as they can tank unboosted Shadow Claw and cripple Arceus with status. Arceus's lack of resistances and weakness to status moves like Will-O-Wisp, Toxic, and Thunder Wave can make it potentially hard to switch onto the battlefield safely. Despite that, Arceus is still one of the best Pokemon in Ubers, and every team must prep for it if they do not want to get easily cleaned by it.

movesets.name: Swords Dance Extreme Killer
movesets.description:
Shadow Claw is Arceus's best option into Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, Giratina-O, and Skeledirge if it does not run Earthquake, making it valuable coverage. Arceus's final moveslot is extremely flexible; Taunt shuts down recovery and status from Pokemon like defensive Arceus formes and Giratina-O and also prevents it from being phazed by Pokemon like Ho-Oh. Recover allows Arceus to negate chip damage, potentially set up multiple times in a game, and also take on Calm Mind Arceus variants. Earthquake allows Arceus to hit Pokemon like Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM for better damage than Shadow Claw. On Silk Scarf and Life Orb sets, Double-Edge is an option to OHKO Gliscor after a Swords Dance and deal heavy damage to opposing bulky Arceus formes. Generally, Arceus most commonly runs Heavy-Duty Boots to negate entry hazard damage, allowing it to sweep more easily. Silk Scarf is an option instead, allowing Arceus to achieve thresholds like OHKOing Miraidon after a Swords Dance and Koraidon after a Swords Dance and layer of Spikes. Although niche, Lum Berry gives Arceus the one-time ability to avoid crippling status from Pokemon like Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, while Leftovers can be used to slightly negate chip damage. Tera Fire is the preferred Tera type, as it allows Arceus to set up against Ho-Oh, check Koraidon and Zacian-C, and become immune to Will-O-Wisp. An alternative is Tera Ghost, giving Arceus the ability to set up on Pokemon like Zacian-C, opposing Extreme Speed Arceus, and Choice Scarf Koraidon. Finally, Tera Normal can be used to boost Extreme Speed, allowing Arceus to achieve thresholds like OHKOing Koraidon and offensive Eternatus after a Swords Dance.

Arceus fits on practically every playstyle, but it best fits on more offensive structures looking for a late-game cleaner that can also potentially operate as a mid-game wallbreaker and revenge killer. One of Arceus's bigger issues is Necrozma-DM, which sponges the majority of its attacks and checks it; Pokemon that can lure in Necrozma-DM and chip it down like Zacian-C and Calyrex-I thus make excellent partners. Other physical attackers like Koraidon and Rayquaza can be good partners to wear down shared checks like Arceus-Water and Arceus-Fairy. Arceus also baits out Terastallization, which is useful to prevent Pokemon like Scale Shot Koraidon from being walled by Tera Fairy. Pokemon like Flutter Mane, Kingambit, and Chien-Pao can all wear down bulky Ghost-types that Arceus struggles with like Giratina-O. Miraidon can take out Pokemon like Ho-Oh, Zacian-C, and Necrozma-DM, all of which Arceus can struggle against. Arceus also appreciates entry hazard support from teammates like Ting-Lu and Gliscor on balance teams and Glimmora and Deoxys-S on hyper offense teams, as they put Koraidon into OHKO range by +2 Extreme Speed.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Between its great natural bulk, ability to boost its Defense with Bulk Up, and singular weakness, Bulk Up Arceus has incredible survivability and is capable of beating many popular physical attackers and walls like Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Fairy. Extreme Speed and Shadow Claw provide nearly perfect neutral coverage in Ubers. With Tera Fire and Taunt, Arceus sets up on nearly every passive and some offensive Pokemon in the tier, most notably turning Ho-Oh and Zacian-C into setup fodder. 56 EVs in Speed allow Arceus to outspeed unboosted Adamant Rayquaza and Kyurem-B while also outspeeding Zacian-C after Sticky Web. Leftovers is the preferred item for its passive recovery, allowing Arceus to comfortably run Taunt, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used with Recover on teams that are susceptible to Toxic Spikes. Do note, however, that this significantly worsens the matchup into Ho-Oh.

This Arceus set fits great on both bulky teams and Sticky Web hyper offense teams as a stallbreaker and sweeper that is difficult for even offensive teams to pick off. On bulky teams, Landorus-T is an excellent partner that can act as a short-term check to Pokemon like Koraidon and Zacian-C, accumulating chip damage on them to the point that Arceus can revenge kill them with Extreme Speed. With Sticky Web support on hyper offense, Bulk Up Arceus gains the ability to outspeed many Pokemon that might give it trouble setting up, most notably Koraidon and Zacian-C. More than many other Pokemon, Bulk Up Arceus hates Toxic Spikes. Thus, Eternatus is an excellent partner, being a remover of Toxic Spikes, Kyogre check, and a sweeper facilitated by Arceus breaking down Eternatus's checks. Checking Miraidon and Kyogre is especially important, as they are among the few Pokemon that can threaten Arceus even if boosted. The aforementioned Eternatus can check Kyogre and remove Toxic Spikes, and Ting-Lu can check Miraidon and set Spikes. Miraidon and Zacian-C can overwhelm defensive Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Water, which can survive even boosted Extreme Speeds and threaten Arceus.

movesets.name: Stall
movesets.description:
Defensive Arceus makes use of its fantastic bulk to wall many offensive tier staples such as Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, Extreme Killer Arceus, Calyrex-I, and Kyurem-B. It can even survive a Close Combat from Zacian-C and cripple it with Will-O-Wisp, though it cannot switch directly into it. Its ability to run Heavy-Duty Boots lets it fit onto teams without dedicated hazard control, allowing it to constantly re-enter the field without being whittled down by hazards. Iron Defense turns Arceus into an excellent physical check, being able to beat many common physical attackers as well as Pokemon such as Koraidon and Zacian-C, which might have coverage against it. Dragon Tail provides phazing and allows Arceus to rack up hazard damage on switch-ins with entry hazards, as well as shutting down sweepers at the cost of HP if they choose to attack instead of using setup moves. While Arceus will not always Terastallize, it can use it to great effect against teams running Koraidon or Zacian-C. Tera Water helps wall Tera Fire Pokemon, as well as resisting attacks such as Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, and Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance. Tera Fairy is an excellent defensive typing that especially improves the matchup against Koraidon. A Bold Nature can be run over Impish if Arceus chooses to run Foul Play as its only damaging move.

Despite the set name, Stall Arceus is not limited only to stall; it can be used on bulky balance teams as well. Regardless of team composition, Arceus requires hazard support from partners such as Gliscor, Clodsire and Necrozma-DM. It also appreciates the support of Knock Off absorbers such as Gliscor to help prevent Arceus from losing its Heavy-Duty Boots, which would leave it vulnerable to hazards. As Foul Play and Will-O-Wisp both target opposing physical attackers, Arceus tends to invite in special attackers such as Miraidon and Kyogre, so it likes to be paired with special walls such as Blissey, Clodsire, or Ting-Lu. Finally, Ho-Oh is another excellent partner, preventing physical attackers from wearing Arceus down with Regenerator and helping it preserve Recover PP. As Arceus cannot take every physical attack, it fits well on teams with other bulky Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Skarmory, Skeledirge, and Dondozo. On more offensive teams, Arceus likes being paired with pivots like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Iron Bundle as well as powerful wallbreakers like Kyogre and Miraidon.

strategies.overview: Arceus is one of the best setup sweepers and revenge killers in AG thanks to its STAB-boosted Extreme Speed. Extreme Speed allows Arceus to act as a revenge killer, making it problematic for opposing setup sweepers like Miraidon and Scale Shot Koraidon. Thanks to its Normal typing and bulk, it can reliably take on Calyrex-S and heal with Recover while forcing Calyrex-S out with Shadow Claw. Physical walls such as bulky Arceus formes and Ho-Oh check Arceus, making it difficult for it to set up and sweep. Arceus struggles with Tera Ghost users such as Koraidon and Miraidon, as they threaten it. Additionally, Zacian-C is a threat, as it beats Arceus with either its boosted STAB moves in Play Rough and Behemoth Blade or Close Combat while Arceus cannot deal any significant damage in return. Arceus is also weak to status moves like Will-O-Wisp, Toxic, and Thunder Wave, making it hard for it to safely switch in. Regardless of these vulnerabilities, Arceus is one of the best Pokemon in AG, and every team must have adequate counterplay for it.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Arceus can opt to run Lum Berry to aggressively set up without worrying about burn and paralysis from Ho-Oh, Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Giratina-O. Lum Berry comes with giving up Heavy-Duty Boots, however, reducing Arceus's longevity by making it difficult to repeatedly switch in on the battlefield. Earthquake used with Tera Fire is a good option on teams that are weak to Zacian-C. On hyper offense structures, Arceus can run Life Orb with Double Edge, allowing it to go wild after a single boost and enabling it to OHKO Ho-Oh before Tera Normal and OHKO Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Landorus-T after. Stone Edge is a niche option to surprise Ho-Oh that OHKOes it at +2, as it likes to switch in on Arceus frequently. Taunt can be used occasionally to stop bulky Arceus formes and Eternatus from phazing Arceus with their status moves and prevents healing with Recover. Taunt also stops Ting-Lu from using Whirlwind to stop Arceus from sweeping and blocks status moves like Will-O-Wisp from Skeledirge and defensive Arceus formes.

Checks and Counters:

Zacian-C: Zacian-C doesn't take significant damage from Arceus's Extreme Speed and unboosted Shadow Claw; meanwhile, it 2HKOes Arceus with Close Combat. However, Arceus can run Tera Fire in conjunction with Bulk Up to set up on Zacian-C.

Koraidon: Koraidon threatens to OHKO Arceus with its powerful Low Kick, runs Tera Ghost to nullify Extreme Speed, and lives +2 Extreme Speed when healthy.

Unaware Users: Arceus is unable to break past Unaware users like Dondozo and Skeledirge, whose solid bulk and access to recovery in Rest and Slack Off let them check Arceus throughout the game, with the latter threatening to burn Arceus with Will-O-Wisp. However, both need to be wary of Taunt, which can prevent them from healing.

Garganacl: Thanks to Purifying Salt backed by great bulk, Garganacl can wall Arceus. Purifying Salt means Arceus cannot do significant damage to it with Shadow Claw. Furthermore, Garganacl can set up Iron Defense to increase the power of Body Press to beat Arceus. However, Garganacl must be wary of Arceus using Earthquake, as +2 Earthquake 2HKOes Garganacl.

Status Moves: Status moves like Toxic from Eternatus and Gliscor and Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave from Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Giratina-O prevent Arceus from safely switching in and hinder its ability to set up in a one-on-one situation against these foes.

movesets.name: Bulky Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Bulky Swords Dance Arceus is one of the best late-game cleaners and revenge killers in the metagame. Its typing and bulk allows it to reliably take on Calyrex-S and heal itself with Recover. Shadow Claw allows Arceus to OHKO Calyrex-S and, at +2, 2HKO Necrozma-DM and Giratina-O. Heavy-Duty Boots increase Arceus's longevity, allowing it to safely come onto the field at any point in time, which makes it a difficult threat to deal with late-game. Tera Fire grants Arceus immunity to burn from Arceus-Fairy's Will-O-Wisp and Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire, allowing it to set up without fear. It allows Arceus to take on +2 Calyrex-S in a pinch, giving it a resistance to Calyrex-S's Grass Knot. Tera Fire also flips the tables on Zacian-C, granting a resistance to both of its STAB moves, which gives Arceus a better chance to take it on. However, the drawbacks of Tera Fire are that it removes Arceus's immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and makes it weak to Earthquake from Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground as well as Arceus-Water's Judgment, being 2HKOed by the latter outside of sun. Tera Normal, on the other hand, boosts Extreme Speed's power to respectable levels, allowing Arceus to OHKO uninvested Miraidon at +2, 2HKO Arceus-Fairy, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Water, and OHKO Koraidon after one layer of Spikes. Furthermore, Tera Normal retains Arceus's defensive utility to check Calyrex-S.

Arceus excels on almost every archetype, fitting best on structures that want a late-game cleaner and revenge killer. Calyrex-S can take advantage of Arceus locked into any move that is not Shadow Claw via Encore and use it as an opportunity to set up Nasty Plot. Choice item Calyrex-S sets like to carry Trick, which cripples Arceus by significantly decreasing its sweeping capabilities. Secondary checks to Calyrex-S such as Ting-Lu and Kingambit are appreciated to share the burden of dealing with it. Furthermore, Ting-Lu can set up Spikes, which assist Arceus in acting as a late-game cleaner by chipping bulky Arceus formes and Koraidon. When unboosted, Arceus is forced out by Miraidon's powerful Electro Drift, so Ting-Lu's ability to take on Miraidon thanks to its bulk and 2HKO it with Earthquake is appreciated. Koraidon can OHKO Arceus thanks to Low Kick, and even when chipped and in range of boosted Extreme Speed, it can use Tera Ghost to avoid being KOed, which often forces Arceus to Terastallize in order to survive Low Kick. Hence, Arceus appreciates walls that can check Koraidon such as Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, Ho-Oh, and Landorus-T. The former two carry Will-O-Wisp to cripple Koraidon, with Arceus-Fairy also scaring it out with Judgment. Ho-Oh can burn Koraidon with Sacred Fire or 2HKO it with Brave Bird. Landorus-T, meanwhile, likes to carry Rocky Helmet to chip Koraidon. Arceus also struggles with Zacian-C, as it cannot break through with either Extreme Speed or Shadow Claw, making Arceus-Water and Landorus-T good partners because they help check Zacian-C. Arceus-Water resists Behemoth Blade and can burn Zacian-C with Will-O-Wisp, while Landorus-T can nullify its Intrepid Sword with Intimidate, chip it with Rocky Helmet, and 2HKO it with Earthquake. Additionally, Choice Scarf Koraidon and Calyrex-S can revenge kill Zacian-C. Arceus finds it difficult to break through staple defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Arceus-Fairy, and Arceus-Water. Consequently, special attackers such as Calyrex-S and Miraidon are great teammates to pair with Arceus. Miraidon can beat these checks with its raw power and access to Electro Drift, while Calyrex-S can break through them with a variety of options such as Nasty Plot + Astral Barrage or Choice item sets. Furthermore, Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy and Kyogre can also beat the aforementioned checks, as well as Ting-Lu, which can stop Arceus from sweeping with Whirlwind if healthy, and, with Tera Poison, Eternatus, which otherwise can Toxic Arceus and put it on a timer.

movesets.name: Bulk Up
movesets.description:
Bulk Up Arceus is a potent late-game setup sweeper and revenge killer that leverages Extreme Speed—the strongest priority move in the tier. Shadow Claw allows it to hit Calyrex-S, Tera Ghost Koraidon, and Giratina-O. Recover allows Arceus to set up on Pokemon such as other Arceus lacking Bulk Up, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, various defensive Arceus formes lacking Will-O-Wisp, and Koraidon after Terastallizing. Tera Fire gives Arceus a burn immunity, which lets it set up on Pokemon that would otherwise check it, such as support Arceus formes with Will-O-Wisp and non-Whirlwind Ho-Oh. It also grants a resistance to Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot at the cost at the cost of Arceus's immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage. Arceus's Special Defense and HP EVs allow it to survive a +2 Tera Grass Calyrex-S Grass Knot or a +2 Tera Stellar Psychic from the same foe. Its Speed creeps it above fully invested, neutral-natured base 90 Pokemon such as Kyogre and Ho-Oh.

Bulk Up Arceus applies offensive pressure on Pokemon such as Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and defensive Ho-Oh, forcing them to stay at high enough HP to successfully stop a sweep. Its longevity relative to regular Extreme Killer Arceus makes it much more prominent on bulkier balance and bulky offense teams, where it frequently acts as a great Calyrex-S check and often threatens to sweep once the opponent's defensive Arceus formes and Ho-Oh are worn down. Bulk Up Arceus struggles with special wallbreakers, like Miraidon and Kyogre, as it can't OHKO them without multiple boosts, allowing them to force out or heavily damage it. Thus, Eternatus is a great partner for Bulk Up Arceus, leveraging its Water resistance to be one of the best Kyogre switch-ins, as well as spreading poison with Toxic Spikes and Toxic. Ting-Lu, being balance's best and only Miraidon check, is also a great partner to Bulk Up Arceus due to its Electric immunity and great Special Defense. Before Terastallizing, Arceus is also weak to Koraidon's Low Kick and burn inflicted by defensive Arceus formes, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O. Arceus-Fairy is a great burn absorber, can force out Ho-Oh with Power Gem, acts as a great Koraidon switch-in, and easily spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave to make it easier for Arceus to set up. Arceus-Water is also a great switch-in to Ho-Oh, leveraging its Fire resistance and threatening it out with Judgment. It also helps slow down Zacian-C, using its Water typing to resist Behemoth Blade and threatening Zacian-C with Will-O-Wisp but at the cost of letting opposing Koraidon use Low Kick more freely than Arceus-Fairy. Bulk Up Arceus is a deadweight against stall due to Dondozo, Skeledirge, Skarmory, and Garganacl walling it effectively. Thus, it appreciates stallbreaking teammates, such as Miraidon and Calyrex-S, which also assist in breaking Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water. Zacian-C also proves to be a challenge for Bulk Up Arceus to break on its own, so it usually relies on teammates such as Ho-Oh or the aforementioned Arceus-Water to force Zacian-C to switch out and slowly chip it with entry hazard damage. Choice Scarf Koraidon is also a great offensive check to Zacian-C and Miraidon, threatening OHKOes with Flare Blitz and Outrage, respectively.

movesets.name: Divine Retribution (Extreme Killer)
movesets.description:
• Arceus has arrived to take its rightful place as the undisputed king of Battle Stadium Singles, unleashing the true power of Extreme Speed in ways Dragonite could only dream of.

  • Swords Dance versus Dragon Dance: Swords Dance allows Arceus to boost its Attack to near unwallable levels with just one turn, while Dragon Dance grants it a Speed boost to better make use of its coverage moves.

  • Shadow Claw: Shadow Claw allows Arceus to break through otherwise problematic Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake doesn't threaten Ghost-types as much as Shadow Claw, but it allows Arceus to hit other problematic foes such as Archaludon much harder.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is great for making quick work of Dondozo, which is otherwise a fantastic foil to most setup sweepers.

Other options

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Arceus to prevent its targets from recovering off its hits, making it much harder for bulkier teams to deal with.

Items

  • Silk Scarf: Silk Scarf is perhaps the most sensible item for Arceus, boosting the already unfathomable power of its Extreme Speed with no downsides whatsoever.

  • Life Orb: While the recoil can be annoying, Life Orb provides a boost to all of Arceus's attacks, making it an even more potent cleanup artist.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry grants Arceus more freedom in finding opportunities to set up by shrugging off otherwise ruinous status like burns from the likes of Ho-Oh, allowing for more liberal use of Arceus throughout the game.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb is useful as a last resort against Encore Calyrex-S.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Arceus will almost never need to terastallize, but it does nonetheless make fantastic use of terastallization.

  • Normal: Tera Normal Arceus is a sweeper of unmatched magnitude, performing astonishing feats of power such as 2HKOing maximum HP Ho-Oh.

  • Ghost: While Tera Ghost offers limited offensive utility, it shines as a defensive Tera option by granting Arceus an immunity to Extreme Speed from opposing Arceus as well as the many Fighting-type attacks aimed at it, such as Koraidon's Close Combat.

  • Fire: Tera Fire hampers Arceus's defensive utility somewhat but gives it a valuable immunity to burn, allowing it much more freedom against bulkier teams.

EV Spreads

  • 212 HP / 252 Atk / 44 Spe with Adamant: This Spread maximizes power while letting Arceus outspeed up to Jolly Dragonite.

  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 108 Spe with Adamant: Dragon Dance variants of Arceus should consider investing more into Speed to more liberally use their non-Extreme Speed moves; this spread lets Arceus outspeed up to Calyrex-S after a boost and Choice Scarf users such as Koraidon at +2.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: Using max Speed sacrifices the power and survivability of slower spreads to make the most of Arceus’s incredible auxiliary movepool.

movesets.name: Extreme Killer
movesets.description:
With strong base stats, Arceus can focus on using Swords Dance and Extreme Speed as a cleaner at the end of a game or as a wallbreaker in the middle of the game to set its teammates up for success. With Extreme Speed's priority, EVs in Speed are unnecessary, barring potential investment to outspeed some Pecharunt and Great Tusk, allowing Arceus to use them in HP to tank hits in situations where it needs to boost or use coverage. The fourth move of choice will depend on what Arceus's needs are and what its team can handle for it. Shadow Claw is used against foes like Air Balloon Pecharunt and Arceus-Ghost, Earthquake is used to hit Pokemon like Eternatus and Garganacl, and Flare Blitz can remove Steel-types like Skarmory and Corviknight. Terastallization, similarly, will depend on what Arceus is most worried about, with Tera Ground and Tera Fire preventing paralysis and burn, respectively, on non-Lum Berry variants alongside the potential STAB boost on coverage; Tera Ghost flipping the script on Pecharunt, Fighting-types, or IronPress users; and Tera Normal increasing the power of Extreme Speed.

Arceus is a versatile god that is able to take any slot that a team needs it to take. With perfectly balanced stats, it cannot meet the astronomical highs that most gods can donate to a stat or two, it provides a respectable boost in offensive stats, above-average defensive boosts for HP receivers like Rotom-Wash, and defensive stats for teammates like Clodsire and Clefable that appreciate having high bulk on both sides. However, base 120 offensive stats are limiting, so receivers that do not desperately need a standout boost, such as Meowscarada or Hisuian Electrode, can take those slots. Arceus should not be placed in Speed, as it would waste the boost by mostly using Extreme Speed; however, it can be positioned in any other slot. Balance teams appreciate Arceus, as it can serve as a win condition for a team otherwise missing one while often appreciating consistent stat donations and revenge kills on wallbreakers like Kyogre and Lokix. Arceus appreciates teammates like Landorus and Rotom-Wash that can force out strong defensive options that don't mind Extreme Speed like Pecharunt, Skarmory, and Clodsire via super effective special attacks.

movesets.name: Extreme Killer
movesets.description:
• With its sheer power, decent bulk, and solid movepool options, Arceus defines itself as one of the tier's most devastating setup sweepers, wallbreakers, and revenge killers. Terastalization, whether it be Normal or Ghost, makes Arceus even more difficult to answer for balance and bulky offense teams due to either its extreme power or improved trading capabilities with would-be revenge killers. Due to it not requiring specific support to function effectively, it is a staple for various hyper offense structures that appreciate a bulky setup sweeper that works well against opposing hyper offense teams.

  • Extreme Speed lets Arceus clean through weakened teams, since not many viable Pokemon resist or are immune to it. Combined with Swords Dance, Arceus can clean up the majority of the offensive metagame, including threats such as Eternatus, Ultra Necrozma, and Sucker Punch Yveltal. Shadow Claw synergizes perfectly with Extreme Speed, hitting Ghost-types such as Giratina-O, Marshadow, and Lunala, which are immune to Extreme Speed, and preventing them being reliable checks to Arceus.

  • Double-Edge makes the most out of the limited number of foes that can switch into Normal-type moves to enhance Arceus's wallbreaking capabilities. It is able to OHKO defensive Ho-Oh and defensive Primal Kyogre after a boost. With Tera Normal, it can also OHKO Coil Zygarde at +2, preventing it from being a consistent check.

  • Taunt denies status conditions from Giratina-O, Alomomola, and support Arceus formes as well as opposing setup from slower foes such as Coil Zygarde and IronPress Garganacl. It has good merit for hyper offense teams too, denying Defog from Ho-Oh and the aforementioned Giratina-O.

  • Recover is a niche option that lets Arceus shrug off attacks, such as Giratina-O's Draco Meteor, Choice Specs Lunala's Moonblast, and support Arceus's Judgment; it notably let Arceus beat Thunder Wave variants of Giratina-O due to its Special Attack drops. However, Arceus is usually better off just attacking instead of using Recover, especially compared to the usefulness of Taunt.

  • Earthquake is another niche option for Sticky Web teams over Double-Edge or Taunt, letting Arceus OHKO Zacian-C after a boost while hitting Garganacl. However, this is very specific because +2 Tera Normal Double-Edge has a roll to OHKO the former, even if Earthquake is better for Tera Ghost variants that do not use Double-Edge.

  • Silk Scarf gives Arceus a consistent damage output to Extreme Speed and Double-Edge that doesn't suffer from the recoil issues of Life Orb, giving Arceus improved longevity while still letting it OHKO offensive Primal Kyogre and Rayquaza with Extreme Speed after a boost.

  • Alternatively, Life Orb maximizes Arceus's offensive capabilities, allowing it to OHKO offensive Eternatus and offensive Ho-Oh after a boost. Unlike Silk Scarf, it improves the power of Shadow Claw as well, notably letting Arceus OHKO Giratina-O and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM with +2 Tera Ghost Shadow Claw. However, the recoil hinders Arceus's longevity significantly, making it less capable of trading with other offensive threats, since it often faints itself from recoil.

  • Lum Berry can also be considered, since it enables easier setup against Ho-Oh, Alomomola, and Giratina-O. Unfortunately, it is too matchup-dependent, and the drop in power is very noticeable, making Arceus less threatening as a whole.

  • The first EV spread lets Arceus outspeed Adamant Kyurem-B as well as Marshadow and Zacian-C after Sticky Web. The rest is dumped into bulk, notably letting Arceus survive Mega Salamence's boosted Double-Edge from full HP. The second EV spread lets Arceus outspeed Chi-Yu while having enough bulk to survive Primal Kyogre's Origin Pulse and Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost from full HP.

  • Tera Normal allows boosted Arceus to OHKO Double Dance Primal Groudon with Extreme Speed after Stealth Rock damage, as well as OHKOing defensive Yveltal and offensive Eternatus. It also empowers Double-Edge, letting it OHKO Zygarde and defensive Primal Groudon at +2 while even having a chance to 2HKO Dondozo. However, it lacks any defensive qualities unlike Tera Ghost and makes Giratina-O and Marshadow more difficult to handle, limiting its use to Sticky Web teams where Marshadow is no longer an issue.

  • Tera Ghost forces Marshadow to play a coinflip between its STAB moves, making Arceus more challenging to punish. It completely shuts down revenge killing attempts from Close Combat Zacian-C, Ditto, and Rayquaza. Offensively, it empowers Shadow Claw, notably letting boosted Arceus OHKO Choice Specs Lunala with Shadow Shield up as well as Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM with Life Orb.

  • Arceus lacks any notable defensive qualities outside of its raw bulk, limiting it just to hyper offense structures that want to capitalize on its fabulous wallbreaking and cleaning abilities. Depending on the moveset, Terastalization option, and opposing team structure, Arceus fluctuates between these two roles.

  • Double-Edge variants of Arceus are more suited to the early- or mid game where it can break through Pokemon such as defensive Ho-Oh and Coil Zygarde for teammates to profit from, especially since its poor longevity makes it difficult to trade with opposing offensive Pokemon or act as a sufficient sweeper.

  • Yveltal is a fantastic partner for Arceus, since it is able to threaten common checks to Arceus, such as Giratina-O, Zygarde, and Ferrothorn, while still being great at breaking past other physical walls such as defensive Primal Groudon and defensive Arceus-Dark. In return, Arceus helps break past specially defensive Pokemon such as Arceus-Fairy, Ho-Oh, and Fezandipiti. They are both capable of overwhelming a shared check in Zacian-C, with other offensive teammates such as Primal Groudon handling that further.

  • Zacian-C itself is a good partner, since it helps Arceus to overwhelm physical walls such as defensive Primal Groudon and Tera Water Zygarde. Zacian-C can help break through Giratina-O, similarly to Yveltal, as well as helping against opposing Arceus and Ditto attempting to revenge kill Arceus. They can both overwhelm a shared check in Necrozma-DM too.

  • Arceus fails to do anything meaningful against stall teams, since both Dondozo and Giratina shut it down with ease. On structures utilizing Sticky Web, Chi-Yu is a fantastic wallbreaker for Arceus, since it notably shreds through stall with its boosted attacks while still beating opposing Ghost-types such as Lunala and Giratina-O. It can even lure in and remove defensive Ho-Oh with +2 Black Hole Eclipse, letting Arceus clean through opposing teams more smoothly. Chi-Yu's fast Taunt helps maintain entry hazards for Arceus too, especially against Giratina-O.

  • Meteor Beam Lunala and Eternatus are very similar when it comes to wallbreaking, letting Arceus clean up better afterwards. Ultra Necrozma appreciates Arceus breaking past both Arceus-Dark and Yveltal, while it can blow through Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon with Earthquake.

  • Suicide leads such as Deoxys-S and Glimmora provide entry hazards for Arceus to break through teams more easily, notably guaranteeing the OHKO on defensive Primal Groudon with +2 Tera Normal Double-Edge and letting Arceus more reliably OHKO Lunala with Shadow Claw once Shadow Shield is removed. Sticky Web support from Smeargle and Shuckle enables Arceus to outspeed foes such as Marshadow and Zacian-C, that would ordinarily revenge kill it.

  • These leads appreciate Arceus using Taunt to maintain their hazards. It should be noted that, barring Shuckle, they can prevent opposing hazards from going up, improving Arceus's longevity, which is especially important for Life Orb or Double-Edge variants.

movesets.name: Trick Room Setter
movesets.description:
• Due to its excellent bulk and Normal typing, Arceus is an excellent Trick Room setter. These qualities combined with a Mental Herb make it extremely difficult for threats such as Primal Kyogre, Zacian-C, and even Marshadow to stop Trick Room from being set up. Arceus also serves as a weak but useful revenge killler that can take out extremely chipped threats such as Primal Groudon and Yveltal with Extreme Speed.

  • Taunt prevents slow entry hazard setters such as Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon from setting hazards. It also prevents threats such as Necrozma-DM and, most importantly, Coil Zygarde from setting up or hindering it with Thunder Wave or Glare. In addition, Taunt prevents Ho-Oh from using Whirlwind to cancel Trick Room or from using Defog to remove entry hazards.

  • Extreme Speed allows Arceus to revenge kill any weakened targets that a teammate wasn’t able to finish off such as a defensive Primal Groudon; however, the lack of Attack investment makes Extreme Speed extremely weak, so the move should not be used often.

  • The given EV spread avoids an OHKO from Choice Band Marshadow’s Low Kick and a 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal’s Dark Pulse.

  • Tera Steel prevents Glimmora and Smeargle from using Mortal Spin to clear entry hazards. Tera Ghost is more niche, allowing Arceus to set Trick Room against Extreme Speed Arceus in an emergency. However, Arceus is a poor user of Terastallization and it should be saved for teammates such as Calyrex-I or Melmetal.

  • Arceus is an excellent Trick Room setter throughout the game thanks to its giant bulk allowing it to set up Trick Room against nearly any unboosted threat. However, it is not to be used as the lead Trick Room setter due to its inability to deny entry hazards from opposing leads such as Deoxys-S, Mental Herb Shuckle, and Mega Diancie.

  • Pokemon that appreciate Trick Room support such as Calyrex-I and Melmetal make excellent teammates for Arceus. They also appreciate Arceus denying Necrozma-DM from using Morning Sun and Zygarde from using Coil and Rest, allowing them to wallbreak past these threats more efficiently.

  • Arceus appreciates additional Trick Room setters to support it in setting Trick Room and preventing entry hazards. Therefore, Hatterene and Cresselia make excellent teammates. Hatterene is able to deny entry hazards from most leads such as Shuckle, Deoxys-S, and Mega Diance, unlike Arceus. Cresselia is also able to restore the PP of teammates with low-PP STAB moves such as Melmetal and Calyrex-I.
